forecast-period.text: A high pressure system over the Tasman Sea extends a ridge across southern SA. A trough of low pressure approaches the western border on Wednesday then moves across the west and north of the State on Thursday and eastern parts on Friday. A ridge of high pressure extends into the west later Friday and over the weekend.
For latest warnings go to www.bom.gov.au, subscribe to RSS feeds, call 1300 659 210* or listen for warnings on relevant TV and radio broadcasts.
* Calls to 1300 numbers cost around 27.5c incl. GST, higher from mobiles or public phones.

Showers and thunderstorms about the Flinders and Pastoral districts and in the west, possibly severe in the far north and far west. Maximum temperatures above average and well above average about the southeast, grading to below average in the west and north. Generally southeast to northeasterly winds, fresh and gusty at times in the north.

Possible showers and thunderstorms about the west, possibly severe in the far northwest and southwest. East to northeasterly winds, tending moderate to fresh and gusty northeast to northwesterly in the west ahead of a south to southeasterly change in the southwest later.

Possible showers and thunderstorms about central and eastern districts, possibly severe in the far east. Maximum temperatures above average, about the agricultural areas grading to below average in the west and north. East to northeasterly winds in the east, with southwest to southeasterly winds extending throughout during the day.
Showers about the agricultural area. Maximum temperatures near average about eastern parts, grading to below average in the west. Southwest to southeasterly winds, fresh at times near coastal parts.

text.p: Light showers about the southern agricultural, most likely about southern coasts and ranges. Maximum temperatures below average. Fresh south to southwesterly winds.

Cumulative rainfall totals to the end of Sunday: Generally less than 5 mm about the agricultural areas, 2 to 10 mm elsewhere increasing to 10 to 20 mm west of about Ceduna to Coober Pedy, north of Coober Pedy, the Flinders district and near the eastern border. Local falls of 30 to 50 mm possible with thunderstorms mainly about the Pastoral districts.
